content:
Your description of what happens is vague. I will assume you mean that the folder opens but nothing appears to be in it.

In a POP3 account, everything is local, even when in the account section. Depending on how you have it set up, some things in the Inbox may still be on the server, but not any of the other folders. That's a disadvantage of POP accounts - the only copy of the messages are on your computer, which means if you don't take care to back them up, and something goes wrong, which is inevitable with computers, your precious email may be lost forever.

The first thing you should do is make a backup copy of your Thunderbird Profile, so you can recover is things go wrong. See this article:

Export your Thunderbird Profile https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/thunderbird-export

When that's done...

- Make sure none of the Quick Filters are enabled. They can hide messages that are really there.

Quick Filter Toolbar https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/quick-filter-toolbar

- Also, try to search for a known message using the Global Search feature:

Global Search https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/global-search

- If you are convinced that the messages are truly not available, and maybe they've been deleted...

-- Check the Trash folder

-- If you thing they may have been accidentally deleted, you can try the "Undelete" add-on:

https://www.ggbs.de/extensions/Undelete.html

- If that doesn't help, it could be a corrupt folder. Try right-clicking on the folder name in the Folders List and choosing "Repair Folder". Follow that up with compacting the folder - right-click the folder name and choose "Compact Folder".

If all those fail, then you probably have lost it all. Sorry. Consider making regular backups.

In the profile there is a prefs.js.msf and a prefs-1.js.msf both dated 2013 (probably when I installed TB). There is also a sub-folder in the profile called Prefs and it contains 38 files starting prefs.js then prefs-1, prefs-2 etc with dates covering the last 10 years. Your case is particular since it is only one - and always the same account - which disappears. In the German and French Thunderbird forums I got accustomed to solve problems where ALL accounts in a profile disappear on Thunderbird start. This mostly happens after a PC or a Thunderbird crash or a power outage, when Thunderbird cannot rewrite the prefs.js file and ad hoc creates a new "virgin" prefs.js file while the old corrupted file is renamed in prefs-1.js (or sometimes in invalidprefs.js).

But in your Thunderbird profile there is something foul. Normally there is only one prefs.js file in the profile folder, and this file is permanently rewritten each time you change a preference (e.g. delete a mail account), when you close and when you start Thunderbird (see timestamps in my attached image). So your profile folder should NOT contain a prefs folder nor any prefs.js.msf files. Unfortunately I don't know whether this is the cause of your disappearing email account on each Thunderbird restart or whether it is the antivirus software or another still unknown cause in the profile.

Next thing I would try - Thunderbird closed - is to delete the prefs folder and all prefs.js.msf, then restart Thunderbird. If your problem still returns and if it were my computer I would uninstall McAfee. But I know that most Windows users are reluctant to do this even if they still have the Windows Defender. So my last proposal is to test creating a new profile, set up only the problematic account and quit and restart Thunderbird several times to be sure that the account works flawlessly in the new profile https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profile-manager-create-and-remove-thunderbird-profiles
